caption:
The tool that clears up thick accents in real time — for the listener, not the speaker.

Krisp is the AI layer that sits quietly between your mic and speakers and whatever call app you're using — Zoom, Meet, Teams, Discord, even regular phone calls. It strips out the small daily friction of calls: the typing noise, the street sounds, the person yelling in the next room, the moment you have to ask "sorry, can you repeat that?"

It just shipped something genuinely new: real-time, listener-side Accent Conversion. The speaker's voice is untouched — nothing is changed on their end. On your end, their voice is rendered clearer and more neutral, processed entirely on your own device. It's a deliberate design choice to sidestep the real criticism that accent-modification tech pressures people to erase how they sound — here, only the listener's experience changes. SiliconANGLE covered the launch, and there are hands-on reviews of people testing it on their own calls.

Beyond that headline feature, Krisp also quietly handles noise cancellation, cancels out other people's voices near you (not just background hum), and runs an AI meeting assistant that transcribes and summarizes calls with no bot joining, no plugin, formatted to the type of meeting you were in — standup, one-on-one, discovery call.

Worth knowing: Accent Conversion currently covers a limited set of accents, with more promised over time, and it's strongest on desktop right now. It's an early slice of a bigger idea, not a universal fix yet.

Krisp's beta hit #1 on Product Hunt and top 3 on Hacker News, and independent reviewers keep landing on the same verdict: it does the unglamorous basics — noise removal, transcription, notes — really well.

slides.heading: The tool that clears up thick accents in real time
slides.body: Not for the speaker — for you, the listener. And it's already shipping.

slides.heading: Every call has the same small tax on your attention
slides.body: Background noise, someone talking over a bad connection, straining to parse an accent, then writing up notes after.

slides.heading: It mutes the room, not just the mic
slides.body: Krisp's noise cancellation filters out typing, traffic, and chatter so only your voice comes through.

slides.heading: It even cancels out other people talking near you
slides.body: Not just hums and clicks — actual competing voices in the room, so the call doesn't get confused mid-conversation.

slides.heading: It writes the meeting up before you've closed your laptop
slides.body: No bot joins the call. It transcribes and summarizes automatically, with action items and templates matched to the meeting type.

slides.heading: It can make a thick accent easier to hear — instantly
slides.body: On-device, listener-side only. The speaker sounds exactly the same to everyone else; only your ears get the clearer version.

slides.heading: It's early, and Krisp says so
slides.body: Accent Conversion only covers a limited set of accents so far, and works best on desktop, not mobile yet.

slides.heading: The call that used to end in confusion now just ends
slides.body: Less noise, less repeating yourself, less mishearing — and a summary waiting for you instead of a blank notes doc.

slides.heading: One quiet layer, three annoyances gone
slides.body: Noise, mishearing, and post-call note-taking — handled in the background, on any call app you already use.

slides.heading: Try it on your next call this week
slides.body: Save this post, install Krisp, and see what your calls sound like with the noise turned off.
